arguments.summary: Command and Control (C2) beaconing was detected from internal host 10.0.8.200 to external IP 10.0.5.14. Further analysis revealed the true C2 relay node to be 10.0.1.10, which was using a domain controller as a reverse proxy for malicious traffic. The beaconing matched a Cobalt Strike malleable C2 profile (JA3 hash: e7d705a3286e19ea42f587b344ee6865) with a 60-second interval and 25% jitter. Attempts to block the C2 relay at 10.0.1.10 were denied due to policy restrictions on firewall actions for critical infrastructure. The source host 10.0.8.200 (WS-IT-101) had previously conducted network scanning activity, indicating potential lateral movement or reconnaissance. No malicious payloads were confirmed in sandbox analysis.

arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was confirmed following the compromise of the krbtgt account hash via DCSync (Event ID 4662) from source IP 10.0.5.14 to domain controller 10.0.1.10. The attacker likely established initial access through a compromised user endpoint (WS-FIN-042, 10.0.5.42) exhibiting Cobalt Strike beaconing behavior. Lateral movement was observed via SMB to a file server. Due to the nature of the krbtgt compromise, all Kerberos tickets in the domain are potentially forged, necessitating a full domain-wide credential revocation. Containment actions were denied due to invalid parameters and lack of approval, indicating a critical failure in execution protocols.
